answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and posts key-signed batch to a board, where a pigment seal binds batch, key, and epoch. Auditors recompute seals at the ember checkpoint, so a copied seal fails on mismatch. A proven claim burns bonds, pays the prover 30, and triggers a ripple audit of batches sharing that key, exposing the cluster. The k-th fake pays 70 plus 10; 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and contribute 10,000. A rented-batch ring fails: rented batches carry the owner's pigment seal, so a mismatch proves duplication. An honest identity pays 80 once and recovers 70 after a clean epoch.
